watchme.trigger: Every build inspection — the event that already fires. inspect() shakes the nest over a component and the reachability sieve is one of its meshes, so the closure is computed there anyway; the probe reads the result of that shake rather than re-walking the graph. No clock, no sweep, no second parse of the tree.
watchme.enough: The claim is 'naming the denied capability stops the list growing while naming the innocent did not.' The denominator is what the OLD rule would have cost: under the allowlist, every module newly reachable from inspector.py cost one human widening with a dated comment — six in six weeks, measured. ENOUGH = ten distinct modules have entered inspector.py's transitive closure since this landed while the denied set is unchanged (ten widenings not paid). KILLED IMMEDIATELY, one occurrence sufficing, if the denied set GAINS an entry to keep the tooth honest — the wrong-shape signal firing, which refutes the node rather than dinging it. A closure that never grows at all is NOT a pass: the instrument had no chance to discriminate, and the probe reports that as insufficient rather than as evidence.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact written against THIS ticket's falsifier, carrying the closure as measured (its size and the modules in it), the denied set as declared with its size, and the delta of both against the values recorded at this ticket's PROVED crossing — so the reader sees the two numbers the claim is a relation between, not one number and an assertion.
watchme.nexus: the build inspector's own sieve corpus — the same place the reach bands and the sole_path findings land, because a rule's efficacy is a finding about a rule and belongs where the other findings about rules are.
watchme.consumer: build_inspector, the owner of the fire-path constraint and the only component that can act on a finding that its own separation rule has started drifting. Law 6: the back-edge that re-opens this node is the owner's act, never the probe's.

THE FALSIFIER RUN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is what this component's own gate demands and is stricter than the class default. FORWARD: 28 teeth in cairn/tools/import_sieve/proofs/test_import_sieve.py, green twice bare; the live corpus caught == [] for all three denied doors read separately; corpus 100 proofs / 100 green / 0 red, twice. BACKWARD, and this is the half that carries the weight: with sieve.reaches stubbed to return {}, FIVE teeth fail — including test_unreachable_catches_a_breach_two_hops_down and the real-corpus tooth, whose non-vacuity assert (closure > 5) refuses to go green over an empty walk — while 23 unrelated teeth stay green. And with `import cairn.devices.librarian` planted at cairn/tools/base/address.py, two hops out, the inspector's tooth reds with the whole route (cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector -> cairn.machines.chart.orient -> cairn.tools.base.address); the twelve-name allowlist it replaced returns [] against that same breach. Strictly wider coverage, measured head to head, arrived at without anyone widening a list.

WHAT WAS BUILT. (1) sieve.reaches(graph, start) — BFS forward transitive closure keeping the shortest chain to each file, folding __init__ through module_name, dead-ending on an unresolvable dotted name, raising on a start it never read. (2) A third rule kind `unreachable` inside catches(), guarded by the HollowScan floor because size is checked BEFORE the kind is dispatched — falsifier clause (3) holds for the new kind, not merely for the two that predate it. (3) build_inspector._FIRE_PATH: the DENIED capability declared once at the inspector's own address (13 modules — the graph tree by both its names, 5432, the inference host, and nine network dialers), a fire_path_unreachable sieve, and the roster entry that makes it mesh #20. (4) The allowlist tuple and the five-module reach loop STRUCK from test_inspector_nexus.py; the proof now COMPOSES the declaration, including deriving TREE_DOORS from _FIRE_PATH['modules'] rather than restating it. (5) A probe at cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/does_the_denied_set_stay_put.py, first tenant of a new probes/.

THE TWO THINGS I WAS WRONG ABOUT, AND MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. (a) I predicted _SOLE_PATH already covered the inference host so the fire-path rule need not name it. Planting `import cairn.devices.inference_domain.route` leaves _SOLE_PATH GREEN — inference_domain is precisely the component permitted to dial — while the verdict path gains the ability to ask an LLM. WHO MAY DIAL and WHAT THE VERDICT MAY REACH are different questions and the second is not implied by the first. (b) I predicted the new sieve would mirror sole_path_holds exactly, including its per-row attribution. It does not. Per-row attribution rebuilt a 243-file graph 24 times, added 22s to every inspection and timed out this component's own proof at 120s; re-read afterwards, the analogy was wrong on the merits too — sole_path's constraint binds EVERY component, this one binds ONE PATH, and that path is build_inspector's.

WHAT THIS CLOSES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. Closes the live trouble the-inspectors-allowlist-tooth-is-red-on-an-import-it-never-admitted: cairn.tools.base.nest stopped being an unmade decision without anyone having to decide it, which is the whole shape of the fix. Does NOT close the bet that the denied set stays put while the closure grows — that needs corpus time and left here as the WATCHME, not as a criterion. Left standing and named: reach_of bands stop at the module boundary, so the two tree-walking sieves band 0 and the nest runs its most expensive meshes first; the dynamic-import check still names 5 modules by hand while the closure holds 17; a subprocess dials and imports nothing (filed edge (b), unchanged).
